messages:
Maya S (Sales): Hey team — FinTech SIG reviewer pinged asking for concise encryption answers they can paste into the questionnaire. Focus: in-transit, at-rest, BYOK options, HSM attestations, rotation policy, and how we prove we never see plaintext CMKs. They also want a short POC checklist. Need copy by EOD.
Evan R (Solutions): Got it. I'll draft two short blocks: a customer-facing summary and a CAIQ/checkbox style paragraph.
Priya D (Security): Quick facts: TLS 1.3 mandatory; optional mTLS for Private; at-rest AES-256-GCM; envelope encryption w/ KEK/DEK separation. We support cloud KMS CMEK and on-prem HSMs (KMIP/PKCS#11). For Hosted we can do BYOK via key references/wrapped keys—Redwood never stores plaintext keys. I'll craft wording.
Priya D (Security): ```
CAIQ-friendly encryption summary (pasteable):
- Transit: Client <> Redwood control plane connections use TLS 1.3 with AEAD ciphers and forward secrecy. For Private deployments mutual TLS can be enabled for additional assurance.
- Rest: Data and model artifacts are encrypted at rest using AES-256-GCM. Application-level envelope encryption is employed: data is encrypted with data keys (DEKs) which are themselves encrypted with key-encryption-keys (KEKs) managed in HSMs/KMS.
- Key custody & BYOK: Customers may supply keys via supported integrations (cloud KMS CMEK/EKM, KMIP, PKCS#11). For Hosted BYOK, customers provide wrapped key material or KMS key references; plaintext key material is never exported to Redwood personnel or systems.
- Rotation: We support scheduled and manual rotation. Default rotation cadence is 180 days; customers may configure tighter policies. Rotation uses key versioning and rewrap operations; full re-encryption workflows available upon request.
- Attestation & audit: We can provide HSM attestation artifacts (where supported), KMS provider compliance statements (FIPS/SOC), and detailed operation logs for all key operations. Audit logs are retained per contract.
```
Evan R (Solutions): Also include a 1-line SIG answer: 'Do you allow customer-managed keys?' -> 'Yes. We support customer-managed keys across Dedicated and Private deployments via KMIP/CMEK/PKCS#11; Hosted BYOK via wrapped keys or provider key references. Plaintext CMKs are never exposed to Redwood.'
Sam T (Eng): POC checklist for engineering: 1) Provide test KMS/HSM endpoint + admin test account (or KMS ARN and service account) with permissions: encrypt/decrypt/unwrap/list/getPublicKey; 2) If KMIP/HSM, provide network access (VPN/allowlist) + PKCS#11/KMIP connection info; 3) Provide sample wrapped DEK or proof-of-wrap operation; 4) Test dataset (anonymized) and acceptance criteria (we'll verify encrypt/decrypt and rotation); 5) Expected SLA for the POC and retention window for logs. I'm available to run the tests.
Maya S (Sales): Customer also asked for contract language they can point to that says Redwood cannot access CMKs in plaintext. Any legal-approved snippet?
Priya D (Security): Draft legal wording: "Redwood will not access, export, or persist Customer Master Keys (CMKs) in plaintext. All cryptographic operations involving CMKs shall be performed within customer-controlled KMS/HSM instances or by using customer-supplied wrapped key material. Redwood will only receive key references or wrapped key blobs and will not retain unencrypted key material." Legal may want to refine, but this is what SIGs expect.
Maya S (Sales): They asked about key destruction and backups too.
Priya D (Security): Key deletion: HSMs/KMS provide delete mechanisms and deletion logs/attestations where supported by vendor. Backups are stored encrypted and keys protecting backups are subject to the same BYOK/KMS controls; we can provide deletion and backup handling procedures under NDA.
kms-bot: POC template + attestation templates: https://redwood.internal/sales/poc/key-custody-playbook and https://redwood.internal/artifacts/hsm-attestation-templates
Evan R (Solutions): Note for Hosted customers needing cryptographic separation, recommend envelope encryption + tokenization pattern; we can include sample IaC for minimal IAM perms in the playbook.
Maya S (Sales): Thanks all — I'll assemble these answers and send to the SIG reviewer. I'll flag if they want the POC.
